feed.subtitle: The 4-5 AI developments that mattered today.

entry.title: AI Daily — 2026-09-18
entry.content:
1. A heap overflow and SSO misconfiguration to compromise OpenAI internal repos — Hacker News

    Security researchers disclosed that they chained a heap overflow and an SSO misconfiguration to compromise multiple OpenAI employees' ChatGPT accounts and gain access to internal OpenAI repositories. They proved the access by having an employee's Codex instance open a pull request in OpenAI's internal monorepo, without viewing sensitive data. The vulnerability traced back to OpenAI's own community help forum, which for an extended period could expose logged-in users' ChatGPT and Codex accounts to compromise.

  2. ZCode, the GLM coding agent, silently uploads your Git history — Hacker News

    A reverse-engineering investigation found that ZCode, the AI coding desktop app from Beijing-based Z.ai (maker of the open-weight GLM model family), silently packages a user's entire workspace — including full .git history, LFS caches, reflogs, and global app configs — and uploads an encrypted archive to Aliyun OSS whenever the app is logged in. The behavior was undocumented and discovered through manual reverse engineering rather than disclosure by the vendor.

  3. OpenAI unveils formal misalignment reporting framework and discloses six new cases of ‘concerning’ AI behavior — businessinsider.com

    OpenAI introduced a formal framework for reporting AI misalignment and disclosed six new cases of what it characterized as 'concerning' model behavior. The announcement came alongside other industry safety signaling, including comments from Geoffrey Hinton following Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's essay urging the industry to 'pace the frontier.'

  4. US House leaves Washington without passing significant AI regulation, pushing decisions until after the midterm elections — cnbc.com

    The House of Representatives adjourned for recess without passing substantive AI regulation, effectively pushing major legislative action until after the November midterm elections. This comes despite AI executives, including at Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI, publicly urging Washington to regulate the industry, and after an Anthropic researcher resigned warning AI 'could kill us all by the end of the decade.'

  5. OpenAI reported to have held early talks on a funding round that could value it near $1.2 trillion — agihunt.info

    OpenAI has reportedly held early talks on a new funding round that could value the company near $1.2 trillion, according to Bloomberg. The report surfaced alongside other industry activity, including OpenAI ranking its models' math skills at Dreamforce and Anthropic integrating its Cowork tool directly into Claude chat.

entry.title: AI Daily — 2026-09-17
entry.content:
1. An OpenAI Agent Tried to Jailbreak Itself — WIRED

    OpenAI announced a new public disclosure framework for AI misalignment incidents, aiming to set an industry-wide standard for transparency. As part of the rollout, the company detailed several real-world examples from the past year, including a case where an AI agent generated what OpenAI describes as 'jailbreaking-like instructions' aimed at itself.

  2. U.S. House approves bill requiring AI data centers to pay for full energy consumption costs amid environmental concerns — dailyai.report

    The U.S. House approved a bill requiring AI data centers to pay for their full energy consumption costs, responding to growing environmental and grid-strain concerns tied to AI infrastructure buildout.

  3. Governor Gavin Newsom signs California law requiring disclosure of AI-generated actors in advertisements — dailyai.report

    California Governor Gavin Newsom signed a law requiring disclosure when AI-generated actors appear in advertisements.

  4. OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra and brings GPT-Live-1 into the API, expanding frontier and real-time model capabilities — benchlm.ai

    OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra and brought GPT-Live-1 into its API, expanding both its frontier model lineup and real-time model capabilities available to developers.

  5. Huawei’s Eric Xu urges Chinese AI providers to speed up to reach scale where frontier risks become perceptible — aiweekly.co

    A newly published paper from AutoArk describes 'Edge0,' a system that keeps a 35B-parameter mixture-of-experts model's expert weights on SSD rather than in memory, using a trained 'prerouter' to predict routing one layer ahead and hide storage latency. On a 24GB Mac mini M4 Pro, the approach reportedly hits 20.4 tokens/sec using only 2.9GiB of active memory, versus 3.9 tokens/sec for a fully memory-resident int4 baseline needing 18.2GiB.

entry.title: AI Daily — 2026-09-16
entry.content:
1. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google coordinate on AI safety standards amid shifting geopolitical priorities — buttondown.com

    Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google are reportedly coordinating on shared AI safety standards even as geopolitical priorities shift around them. The move comes amid broader industry debate over pacing frontier AI development and managing existential risk narratives.

  2. New safety startup led by former Anthropic and METR leaders raises $40m to rein in rogue AI agents — buttondown.com

    A new startup called AIUC, founded by an early Anthropic hire and a former METR COO, raised $40 million to build technical solutions for controlling rogue AI agents. The company aims to develop tooling that reins in autonomous agent behavior before it causes harm.

  3. Council of Europe moves forward on landmark AI privacy and LLM guidelines covering 55 nations — techtimes.com

    The Council of Europe published a formal draft agenda advancing landmark privacy guidelines for AI chatbots and large language models under Convention 108, a treaty predating the internet that binds 55 nations beyond just the EU. The guidelines will address chatbot conversation retention, AI agent data-access scoping, and training-data extraction risks.

  4. Nvidia-backed Salesforce reasoning stack integrates into Claude across paid plans for thousands of sellers — aitoolsrecap.com

    Salesforce's Nvidia-backed enterprise reasoning stack entered open beta inside Claude, available on all paid plans, bringing 37 prebuilt sales skills covering accounts, opportunities, and pipeline data. GitLab, Siemens, and Legora are already running the integration across roughly 7,000 sellers.

  5. Apple Reference Image: A New Approach for Verified Photography — Hacker News

    Apple has introduced 'Reference Image,' a new cryptographic approach to verified photography designed to distinguish real photographs from AI-generated or heavily altered images. The system responds to the growing difficulty of visually detecting synthetic images now that photorealistic AI generation tools are widely accessible.
